## Context
ADR 0100 makes the immutable route registry and parser factories the authority for command identity, grammar, and committed help. Twenty-one visible pure-intercept routes support `rebar <command> --help` but remain absent from overview help and fail under `rebar help <command>`.

## Plan
- Make the existing help-backed predicate in `scripts/gen_cli_help.py` and `src/rebar/_cli/_help_route.py` exactly `not route.hidden and not route.retired`; do not add a Route metadata field. This includes all twenty-one canonical pure-intercept routes while continuing to exclude hidden aliases and retired spellings.
- Move `_unwrap_usage` and `_collapse_metavars` from `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` into `scripts/gen_cli_help.py`. Apply them inside `render_route` only for `route.group == "intercept"`, before the existing byte normalization, so new intercept artifacts are stable across Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13 while existing non-intercept artifacts retain their byte contract.
- Generate one committed `help/<route>.txt` artifact for each newly help-backed intercept route. The existing `src/rebar/_cli/_help.py` file lookup, `subcommand_help`, and `known_subcommands` then serve and discover those files without a second rendering path.
- Update `_help_route.pre_scan` through its mirrored help-backed predicate so leading or top-level pure-intercept help is served before execution. Keep `_NESTED_FAMILY` behavior unchanged: examples such as `rebar bridge preview --help` and `rebar audit serve --help` still fall through to their nested argparse owners, while `rebar audit --help` remains top-level committed help.
- Delete the live pure-intercept `_render_intercept` path in `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`; make `_syntax_body` use `help_mod.subcommand_help(route.name)` for every documented route and fail if the committed artifact is absent. Thus the reference consumes the exact normalized runtime bytes rather than independently rendering a parser.
- Retain `_OVERVIEW_OMIT` as exactly `bridge-fsck` and `bridge-probe`, the existing documented compatibility entrypoints already advertised under `bridge`. Retain the matching overview-test allowlist as exactly `help`, `bridge-fsck`, and `bridge-probe`; none of the twenty-one pure-intercept routes is exempted from overview membership.
- Regenerate package help, overview help, and the CLI reference through the existing generators.
- Add registry-driven behavioral coverage for every pure-intercept route, exact-byte equality across both top-level help surfaces, generator determinism, reference consumption, and preserved nested-help fallthrough.
- Do not add another router, parser, help source, mechanical writing-policy gate, or change to the Markdown-only reduced test policy.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every live visible route outside the exact documented overview omit set appears exactly once in overview help.
- [ ] `rebar help <command>` succeeds for every canonical pure-intercept route returned by the registry.
- [ ] The registry-driven pure-intercept help test proves no command handler executes.
- [ ] The registry-driven pure-intercept help test proves no ticket store is mounted or created.
- [ ] `rebar help <command>` returns the exact bytes of that route committed artifact.
- [ ] Top-level `rebar <command> --help` returns the exact bytes of that route committed artifact.
- [ ] New pure-intercept artifacts render identically under Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13.
- [ ] Each CLI-reference pure-intercept syntax block equals the corresponding committed artifact rather than a live parser render.
- [ ] `_OVERVIEW_OMIT` and the test allowlist retain only their named existing bridge/help exemptions; no pure-intercept route is exempt.
- [ ] Hidden aliases and retired spellings remain absent from overview discovery.
- [ ] Non-leading nested help for `bridge` and `audit` families retains argparse fallthrough.
- [ ] Help and CLI-reference drift checks pass.
- [ ] No competing routing, parser, help, writing-enforcement, or documentation-test-policy mechanism is introduced.
